hypotheses.claim: ClayCode diagnostics should separate stable rule identity, rule revision, occurrence fingerprint, source spans, presentation/rendering and run-local instance identity; a versioned structured occurrence fingerprint should outperform text/span and rule-only identity for regression and corpus use.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production differential showing that a simpler identity scheme preserves nonsemantic invariance and semantically distinct-cause separation at equal or lower complexity across parser, type/effect, runtime/FFI and lowering diagnostics.

hypotheses.claim: Human-readable diagnostic message text and absolute source positions should be presentation/location evidence, not the stable label used by WP11 fuzz deduplication or WP12 negative/held-out corpus identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: A broad refactor/path/rendering differential where text+position identity remains stable whenever semantic diagnostic identity is unchanged without masking distinct causes.

hypotheses.claim: When a lowered/runtime check preserves a known semantic denial cause, lowering should preserve or link its diagnostic rule/cause identity rather than collapse all failures to an undifferentiated DENY; behavioral outcome equivalence alone is insufficient for diagnostic equivalence.
hypotheses.falsifier: H1/H2 differential evidence showing that generic outcome-only DENY preserves all required debugging, mutation localization, held-out labeling and causal replay information.

hypotheses.claim: Diagnostic fingerprint algorithm version and diagnostic rule semantic revision should be independent version axes: algorithm changes affect matching mechanics, while rule revision changes the predicate/meaning being diagnosed.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production implementation showing one version axis can evolve either concern without false equivalence, false novelty or migration ambiguity.

counterhypotheses.claim: Stable diagnostic identity is premature overengineering for BASE; message plus stage plus source location is sufficient until H1/H2.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Run location/rendering/refactor perturbations over current WP03/WP04/WP11/WP12 negative cases and measure false-new vs false-same classifications.

counterhypotheses.claim: A stable rule_id alone is sufficient; occurrence fingerprints add needless complexity.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Generate multiple simultaneous instances and distinct causal signatures under the same rule; measure collisions and mutation-localization loss.

counterhypotheses.claim: Stable diagnostic IDs ossify checker implementation details and impede refactoring.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Refactor checker/lowering implementation while preserving semantic predicate; verify whether rule identity can remain stable while implementation provenance changes independently.

counterhypotheses.claim: Semantic anchors can create false stability when the underlying cause changes at the same IR node.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Hold rule+anchor fixed and mutate normalized cause signature; compare rule-anchor versus structured fingerprint separation.

promotion: NONE; candidate requires integration against production ClayCode and Ubuntu target-host receipts
